prompt: After the `PUT` lowered the price, why did the next GET still show 8,990?
hint: Who told the cache about the change?

choices.text: The PUT failed to save the new price
choices.why: The shop returned 7,990 and stored it.

choices.text: The database caches values for a minute
Nginx sent that PUT to the other shop instead

prompt: With `max-age=60`, what is the longest anybody can be shown the old price after a change?
hint: The worst case: the copy was taken just before the change.

choices.text: No time at all; the copy updates itself
choices.why: The copy does not know about the change.
The copy expires on its own.
inactive removes unused copies; freshness comes from max-age.

prompt: Which should not go into a shared cache at all?
hint: Wrong for even a second.

choices.why: Right. Personal, and wrong is never acceptable.
It can be cached for a year.

prompt: A team sets every API lifetime to one second "so nothing is ever stale". What do they lose?
hint: The hit ratio and the gap between requests.

choices.text: Nothing at all; one second is free
choices.why: Only requests within the same second are spared.

choices.text: Correctness, since one second is still too long
choices.why: One second is almost always acceptable.

prompt: What does a request with the right `X-Cache-Refresh` token do to the cached copy?
hint: BYPASS, and then a HIT with the new price.

choices.text: Deletes it and stores nothing in its place
choices.why: The next request was a HIT, so something was stored.

choices.text: Extends its lifetime by another minute

prompt: Why does the refresh header need a secret token?
hint: What could a stranger do with the header alone?

choices.text: Nginx rejects headers that carry no value
To encrypt the cached copy on disk
map only works when a token is given to it

prompt: Why can't open-source Nginx simply `PURGE` a URL?
hint: Which edition has the module?

choices.text: PURGE is forbidden by the HTTP standard
choices.why: It is a convention used by many caches.

choices.text: The purge module is in NGINX Plus

prompt: With `levels=1:2`, the copy for key hash `e8fb...6679` lives under which directories?
hint: Taken from the end of the name.

choices.why: From the start; levels count from the end.
Right: the last character, then the two before it.
The second level is the two characters before the last.

prompt: A script deletes the cache file for `https://ipelivros.example/api/books/2`, and the old price stays. What is the likeliest mistake?
hint: Whose name was in the key lesson 5 showed?

choices.text: It hashed the site's URL; the key is http://shop/api/books/2
choices.why: Right. The hash pointed at nothing.

choices.text: MD5 is not supported on Ubuntu

choices.why: The MISS came without any reload.

choices.text: Nginx keeps a second copy in memory
choices.why: Only the index is in memory.

prompt: How does a hashed file name make a long cache lifetime safe?
hint: What happens to the URL when the file changes?

choices.text: A changed file gets a new URL
choices.why: Right. No copy is ever wrong.

choices.text: Nginx compares hashes on every request

prompt: Why was the regular expression `\.[0-9a-f]{8}\.(css|js)$` written in double quotes in the Nginx file?
hint: What does `{` mean to Nginx's parser?

choices.text: Quotes make the matching run faster

choices.why: Only ones with braces or spaces.

prompt: Every asset is hashed and cached for a year as `immutable`. Which file must keep a short lifetime for a new release to reach visitors?
hint: Where does the new name appear?

choices.why: It has a new name; its old copy is never asked for.

choices.text: The HTML page that names the assets

choices.why: A year-old HTML would point at last year's files.

prompt: Both shops were stopped. Why did book 3 get `STALE` with a price and book 4 get `502`?
hint: What did Nginx have for each?

choices.text: Book 4 does not exist in the database
choices.why: It exists; the shop has twelve.
Every book had the same headers.

prompt: With `updating` and `proxy_cache_background_update on`, how long did the first request after expiry take?
hint: STALE, served at once.

choices.text: About 150 ms, the time the shop takes to answer
choices.why: That was the first fetch, before any copy.

choices.text: About 27 ms, a cached answer's time
choices.why: Right. The fetch happened behind it.
The sleep came before the requests.

prompt: Which response should never be served stale during an outage?
hint: Old data that becomes a lie.

choices.why: Seconds-old prices beat an error page.
Right. Keep use_stale out of that location.

prompt: An origin asks caches to serve a stale copy while refetching with `Cache-Control: max-age=60, ___=30`.
hint: Stale, while…

prompt: Put the steps of the race that leaves the old price cached in order.
hint: The read starts first and finishes last.
items: The visitor's read misses the cache
The read gets 8,990 from the database
The read stores 8,990 in the cache
trap: The store at the end is what undoes the purge.

prompt: Which defence limits the damage of the race even if every other defence fails?
hint: The backstop.

choices.why: It narrows the window but can still miss.
Right. The wrong value lives at most one lifetime.
Narrows the window, does not close it.

prompt: Why does the race get more likely under load?
hint: What is the window?

choices.text: Purges are dropped under heavy load

choices.why: Right. The window is that time.
That helps, but the window is the read's duration.

choices.text: TLS handshakes slow the purges down a lot

prompt: Which of these make a changed price visible before the copy expires? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two from this lesson, one that does nothing.

choices.text: A refresh request with the token
A request with a wrong token
choices.why: It is served from the copy.

prompt: A copy with `max-age=60` was stored at 10:00:00, and the price changed at 10:00:20. Without invalidation, for how many seconds is the wrong price served?
hint: Until the copy expires.

prompt: A price appears on the book's page, the listing and the search results, all cached. How many refresh requests does the token method need?
hint: The refresh is per URL.

choices.text: One per URL that shows the price
choices.why: Right. Lesson 7's purge by tag removes this.

choices.text: One, for the book's id, which updates every page at once
choices.why: Nginx knows URLs, not which pages show a book.
Double purging is about timing, not about how many pages.

pairs.right: makes a copy never become wrong
serves an expired copy on purpose

hint: The new HTML names a different file.
